abstract: We compute local residue selectors for generalized Thomas sections. Under contact normalization, the Hessian-null derivative must be supplemented by a zero-order term determined by the transformed volume density and the contact unit. An explicit cubic gives a nonzero correction even for a constant numerator. A section with two $D_4$ singularities integrates this local calculation with a defect-two relation space and detects a specified integral algebraic class through its Saito pairing. Five standalone exact Singular programs and retained outputs support these finite models; the residue matrices are tied to the mathematical derivation. The remaining material provides controlled examples and scope restrictions. A plane-containing cubic fourfold supplies a complete nodal control for the primitive plane class. A specialization of the published rational-root and join construction for fake linear cycles gives an annihilator whose associated hyperplane section is smooth. This refutes only the explicit unrestricted per-member implication from a linear annihilator to singular support, and does not exclude a different detecting member in the same net. No novelty is claimed for fake linear cycles, the complete-intersection period formulas or the general defect machinery. An appendix separates the quadratic-polarization transfer criterion from a mere weight-two Hodge map and records the known Weil-support construction with an additional local-freeness hypothesis. Reflexivity alone does not establish that hypothesis. The results prove no new general case of the Hodge conjecture.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
1. Novelty and attribution narrowed (Section 1, abstract): main contribution stated as the explicit nonzero volume-density correction for a contact-normalized D4 residue selector and its use in the two-D4 detecting section; the fake-linear class of Section 4 is credited as a specialization of the rational-root and join construction of [3, Theorem 7.1 and proof of Theorem 1.1]; fake linear cycles and failure of recovery from periods credited to Duque Franco-Villaflor Loyola [4] (added); the smooth-section observation is presented as an application, not a general obstruction; normal-bundle formula, plane-containing control and Appendix A described as context/established constructions (Appendix A credits [10]).
2. Section 4: 'linear-support inversion' is defined explicitly as the unrestricted per-member implication being tested, and is no longer attributed to the reconstruction literature.
3. Theorem 3.1 item 2: proof now cites the complete-intersection period formula [6, Theorem 1.1] and the period-annihilator identification [7], with the colon-ideal/Gorenstein socle argument; it explains that the plane's nonzero primitive pushforward together with the one-dimensional extra homology identifies the Saito image [2, Theorem 1].
4. Section 6: the broken implication display (stray '$$4pt]' fragments) is replaced by a single aligned display.
5. Added comparison with rStation hodge_conjecture_5 v5 [5] (higher-order Hodge-locus obstructions; no overlap with the local residue calculation).
6. Author/disclosure line standardized; journal data added for [14]. No theorem is strengthened; supplement unchanged.
7. References renumbered in order of first citation (v1 [14],[15] become [4],[5]; v1 [4]-[13] become [6]-[15]).
title: Generalized Thomas Sections and Density-Corrected Residue Selectors
